title: Implement an LRU cache in Python
description: Implement an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache with get/put operations and a fixed capacity.

files.tests/test_lru.py:
from src.lru import LRUCache

def test_basic_put_get():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put(1, 10)
    assert c.get(1) == 10

def test_missing_key():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    assert c.get(99) == -1

def test_eviction():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put(1, 1)
    c.put(2, 2)
    c.put(3, 3)  # evicts key 1
    assert c.get(1) == -1
    assert c.get(2) == 2
    assert c.get(3) == 3

def test_update_moves_to_recent():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put(1, 1)
    c.put(2, 2)
    c.get(1)    # 1 is now most-recently used
    c.put(3, 3) # evicts key 2
    assert c.get(2) == -1
    assert c.get(1) == 1

def test_overwrite():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put(1, 10)
    c.put(1, 20)
    assert c.get(1) == 20

task_spec.prompt:
Implement LRUCache in src/lru.py using an OrderedDict:
- `__init__(self, capacity)`: store capacity, create `self._cache = OrderedDict()`
- `get(key)`: if key missing return -1; else move_to_end(key) and return value
- `put(key, value)`: if key exists, move_to_end(key); set _cache[key]=value; if len > capacity, call _cache.popitem(last=False) to evict LRU
All 5 tests must pass.
